prediction.raw: 0 I think it's wrong to scream at your coworker, even if they were calling you late at night. While it's understandable to feel frustrated and want to set boundaries, screaming is not an effective or respectful way to communicate. It's possible to express your needs and concerns calmly and assertively, without resorting to aggressive behavior. A more constructive approach might be to say, "Hey, I appreciate you reaching out, but I'm not available to talk after [insert time]. Can we discuss this during work hours instead?" This approach sets clear boundaries while maintaining a professional and respectful tone. Screaming, on the other hand, can damage your relationship with your coworker and create a toxic work environment.
